decisions.reason: F2 inaccurately attributes two spherical disk sides directly to a supplier whose Statement concerns the bounded planar disk. This is a nonfatal citation overstatement: the needed planar separation is actually proved in supplier Proof 2.1. F2 now cites that exact argument and derives spherical separation by adding infinity to the unbounded component; the odd transverse-crossing argument and smooth finite-neighborhood construction are valid.

The rejected smoothness objection is false. F4 expressly invokes the proof of F3, whose steps 1.1 and 3.1 construct a smooth boundary component of a finite regular neighborhood; step 2.1 proves it separates graph points. Step 1.1 repeats that construction in a planar chart and uses only the bounded planar Jordan disk, exactly within the actual supplier Statement. Its product with a height interval has a smooth spherical boundary after rounding in a neighborhood disjoint from the compact link; projection points on each side give link points inside and outside. The unused two-spherical-disks description is an elementary consequence: delete a point in either complementary region and apply the planar disk result to the other bounded side. No strengthened lemma Statement is required.

The original step 1.1 infers nonemptiness from connectedness without fixing a convention for vertexless projection graphs, then uses F5 outside its explicit nonempty domain if the empty diagram is admitted. This is a nonfatal omitted boundary case: any empty diagram has zero crossings and immediately realizes the nonnegative crossing minimum. New step 1.1 proves that case directly, and steps 2.1–4.1 retain the nonsplit/connected-competitor and normalized-bracket span argument only for nonempty links. F5 now records the actual nonempty supplier domain and monomial normalization. The theorem Statement and AC_omega assumption are unchanged.
